info.name: RentBook Microservices API
info.description: End-to-end tests for user-service, billing-service and notification-service. Pick an environment (Local or Deployed) and use Run collection. Every run creates fresh accounts, so it can be run any number of times.

item.name: 0. Health & service-to-service connectivity
item.description: Run these first. On Render free tier the first call can take ~50s while a service wakes up.

item.name: Register as admin is downgraded to tenant
3. Bills (billing-service ⇄ user-service)
item.description: Creating a bill makes billing-service call user-service to validate the tenant and the property.

exec: pm.test("tenant name came from user-service", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().tenant.name).to.eql('Nila S'); });

item.name: Issue bill to an owner account → 400
Owner lists bills (names enriched from user-service)

exec: pm.test("routed to the owner who billed this tenant", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().owner).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get('ownerId')); });

item.name: Owner lists complaints (tenant name from user-service)

exec: pm.test("amount due is the pending bill", () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().amountDue).to.eql(7500); });

item.name: 7. Notifications (notification-service, Telegram)
item.description: Events from billing-service land here. Telegram is simulated through the internal endpoint so the suite passes with or without a real bot token.

item.name: Tenant feed has "new bill" and "resolved" alerts

exec: const t = pm.response.json().items.map(n => n.type); pm.test('bill.issued delivered', () => pm.expect(t).to.include('bill.issued')); pm.test('complaint.updated delivered', () => pm.expect(t).to.include('complaint.updated'));

item.name: Owner feed has "payment received" and "new repair" alerts

exec: const t = pm.response.json().items.map(n => n.type); pm.test('bill.paid delivered', () => pm.expect(t).to.include('bill.paid')); pm.test('complaint.created delivered', () => pm.expect(t).to.include('complaint.created'));
